security_audit.summary: The audit confirms the CI template remote installer piped to bash as a critical supply-chain pattern and flags stealth guidance as a high-risk semantic issue. Most other static detections are false positives from Markdown examples, reference links, dummy credentials, and secure coding examples. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote install script piped to shell in CI template
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with a pinned release, checksum verification, or a trusted GitHub Action version.

remediation.issue: Stealth and WAF evasion scan guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion examples or restrict them to approved defensive validation with explicit scope and logging requirements.

remediation.issue: Placeholder credentials in authenticated scan examples
remediation.suggestion: Use neutral placeholders and warn users never to place real secrets in prompts or shared files.

content.value_statement: Web teams need repeatable checks for web server misconfigurations and outdated components. This skill guides authorized Nikto scans and turns findings into practical remediation notes.
actual_capabilities: Explains basic Nikto scans for HTTP, HTTPS, ports, virtual hosts, and authenticated targets.
Shows tuning options for vulnerability classes such as injection, files, disclosure, and server identification.
Guides output generation in text, HTML, CSV, and XML formats for reports.
Provides CI workflow examples for adding web security scans to delivery pipelines.
Maps findings to OWASP, CWE, NIST, PCI DSS, and CIS references.
limitations: It does not grant authorization to scan third-party systems.
Nikto results can include false positives that require manual verification.
Scans can create high traffic and trigger monitoring alerts.
The skill does not replace deeper manual penetration testing.

use_cases.title: Perimeter Web Server Review
use_cases.description: Assess approved internet-facing servers for outdated software, risky files, and basic configuration weaknesses.

use_cases.title: Release Pipeline Security Check
use_cases.description: Add a repeatable web server scan step before deployment or after infrastructure changes.

use_cases.title: Compliance Evidence Collection
use_cases.description: Create scan records, remediation notes, and framework mappings for audit evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a basic Nikto scan for my authorized web server. Include scope checks, safe timing, and report output.

prompt_templates.title: Review Scan Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Nikto findings. Group likely issues, possible false positives, and remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Scan Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a CI web security scan step for an approved test environment. Include artifacts and failure criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Executive Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert Nikto results into an executive summary with risk themes, affected systems, and owner-ready remediation actions.

output_examples.input: Authorized HTTPS server scan with an HTML report requirement.
output: Nikto scan plan with timeout and output settings.
Review steps for validating findings before escalation.

output_examples.input: Nikto report with outdated server software and exposed default files.
output: Prioritized finding summary by business risk.
Suggested owner actions for patching and file removal.
Notes for evidence collection and retesting.

output_examples.input: Need a recurring web security scan in a delivery pipeline.
output: Pipeline design with controlled targets and retained artifacts.
Guidance for manual review before blocking releases.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, and scan windows before running Nikto.
Use rate limits, time limits, and maintenance windows for production-like systems.
Manually validate findings before assigning severity or remediation owners.
anti_patterns: Do not scan systems outside the approved scope.
Do not paste real credentials or session cookies into prompts or shared files.
Do not treat raw scanner output as confirmed vulnerability evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan, run, and document authorized Nikto web server vulnerability scans.

faq.question: Can I scan any public website?
faq.answer: No. Only scan systems you own or have explicit written permission to test.

faq.question: Does Nikto prove a vulnerability exists?
faq.answer: No. Nikto highlights likely issues that need manual verification and business context.

faq.question: Can this skill support compliance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes report structure and mappings to common security frameworks.

faq.question: Will scans affect production systems?
faq.answer: They can. Nikto creates noticeable traffic and should use approved windows and limits.

faq.question: Should I include credentials in prompts?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders and handle real credentials only through approved secret management.
